comments.text: the travelogue's entry, from the shell, which runs it as a subroutine before an event. Stops the CIA timers, sets VIC bank 1, a multicolour bitmap at $6000 with its screen at $4000, black border and background; clears the screen and draws the frame ($1359), writes the event's page of text ($14AB), draws the event's picture ($2411 with the event's number plus one, $081F), starts the raster interrupts at line 0 ($10BF) and draws the globe ($11C1)
the unpacker's read of the header's second byte; here, inside the travelogue's code
the unpacker's read of the header's third byte; here, inside the travelogue's code
the unpacker's read of the header's fourth byte; here, inside the travelogue's code
the shell's unpacker reads the packed file's header here ($1000-$1004 and $10FF) while it unpacks; once it is done, the travelogue's code is here
waits for the fire button on either joystick; there is no time limit
at raster line 0: interrupts off, the interrupt's "screen on" rewritten as LDA #$00 ($117F), the screen blanked, and back to the shell, which loads the event

the raster interrupt at line 0: the bitmap for the top of the screen ($D018 = $09) and the next interrupt at line 114 ($1191). Every fifth frame ($11), with interrupts allowed again, it turns the dot that marks the event's country on the globe's map on or off ($22) and turns the globe a step ($11CC), then switches the screen on

the dot on: keeps the map's two bytes at the event's place ($12E9) in $20 and $21 and writes them back with the event's pixel pattern ($12F9, $1301), at the place and 160 bytes on, in the map's second copy 20 cells round
the shell's unpacker reads the last header offset here before the travelogue's bytes replace it; here, the middle of the interrupt routine
the dot off: the map's two bytes put back from $20 and $21, at both places
turns the globe a step at $61C0, unless the last step is still being drawn ($23 clear): the drawing runs with interrupts allowed, so the interrupt at line 114 can come in the middle of it
ORA #$10 sets the screen-on bit; $10AC rewrites it as LDA #$00 at the end
the operand of the ORA that turns the screen on, which $10B1 replaces with 0
the end of both interrupts: acknowledges the raster interrupt and returns
the raster interrupt at line 114: from here down the screen is text, with the screen at $4400 and the character set at $7000 ($D018 = $1C), for the page about the event; the next interrupt at line 0
the globe's first drawing, at $61C0 (row 1, cell 16), with no step first
turns the globe one step: the next of four positions within a cell ($1B), after four the next cell of the map ($10, counting down from 10 and wrapping from 1 to 20); falls into the drawing

draws the globe: six rows of nine cells from the map at $3000, from cell $10, each byte shifted right by two bits for each position in $1B with the bits from the cell before ($18), ANDed with the row's circle mask ($12DD) into the bitmap at $12/$13. The first time ($1A) it also colours the globe: $15 in the screen at $4038, 6 in colour RAM
the copy of one byte: the map's byte, or the shifted one, ANDed with the mask, into the bitmap: the three $FFFF operands are filled in for each row
the low byte of the map read's operand, written for each row
the high byte of the map read's operand
the low byte of the mask read's operand
the high byte of the mask read's operand
the low byte of the bitmap write's operand
the high byte of the bitmap write's operand
the circle mask of each of the globe's six rows, the bottom row first: 72 bytes each, from $3960 to $3B0F
the masks' high bytes
for each event, the place in the world map at $3000 of the dot that marks its country: weightlifting, barrel jumping, cliff diving, slalom, log rolling, bull riding, caber toss, sumo
the dots' places, high bytes
for each event, the mask that clears the dot's pixel in the map's byte
for each event, the dot's pixel, ORed in where the mask cleared
40 bytes, one for each cell across the screen, written to one pixel row of the bitmap at $68C0 by $13E0: the upper line of the airliner's route
40 bytes for the pixel row two below, at $68C2: the lower line of the route

clears the bitmap ($6000-$69FF) and both screens ($4000-$47FF), sets colour RAM to red (2) for the bitmap's top eight rows and light red (10) below, draws the two lines of the route across row 7 of the bitmap ($1309, $1331), and the frame of the text window in the text screen at $4400 with the frame characters $60-$6E
the page of the clear loop's STA, $60 to $69, stepped by the loop

writes the frame character in A down rows 10 to 23 of the text screen, in the column in Y

writes the event's page ($081F): its 432 characters from the list at $1593, through the table at $15A3, into $B000, then twelve rows of 36 into the text window from row 11, column 2 of the screen at $4400, in white; then the event's name in the frame's top row ($1681), in white; then the airliner's picture ($2411, picture 0)
